rows.evidence: Q1: Material and Methods / Results - the authors ran their own online questionnaire (14 questions) sent to 457 coffee growers in Bahia in 2021, with 34 responses (7.4% return), and report frequencies of answers.
rows.notes: The study is a perception survey of coffee growers about precision agriculture in general (knowledge, use, obstacles, internet connectivity). It reports no measurement, trial or application of remote sensing, geostatistics or spatial variability mapping, and no result on soil management or soil health outcomes. The only soil-related own finding is that 62.1% of respondents think PA is more important for soil management, which is an opinion about PA generally, not evidence that remote sensing delivers effective soil management. The passages on geostatistics, sampling grids, nutrient dosage and soil compaction in the Discussion are summaries of other studies (Ferraz et al., Figueiredo et al., Zanella et al., Jorge et al., Silva et al.) and do not count as the study's own result.

notes: Full text appears complete. The paper is a small (n=34) grower survey with a self-reported 14% margin of error at 90% confidence; it contains no field or remote-sensing data of its own.
